Vibeprint: how does an iPad sketch over the LAN reach the local
coding agent?

New engineers · Direct LAN path only: iPad browser to local daemon, plaintext .vibeprint/ state, and the agent's MCP
server reading marks.
iPad

Local device on same
LAN, user-managed
iPad browser

Draws sketches and
marks, shows chat
Developer machine
One local host: daemon, MCP, files
Daemon

Token-gated canvas
server, owns state
Agent MCP

Process the coding
agent runs for tools
.vibeprint dir

Plaintext canvas,
marks, chat, token

Key: frames = trust/deployment zones; box = runtime actor/process; cylinder = stored state. Arrows: caller →
recipient, response included; solid = sync; dashed = async; dotted = local command/I/O. Flow type is also
written on each arrow.
F1 · iPad browser → Daemon: 2. canvas ops over WS (async)
F2 · Agent MCP → .vibeprint dir: alt: locked file I/O (local)
Token gate

Non-local callers without a
matching token (header, cookie
or ?t=) get 401; WS upgrades are
refused too.
Source: src/server/daemon.ts
No daemon: files mode

MCP edits .vibeprint/ under
files.lock; waits 5s then 503, locks
older than 10s count as stale.
Source: src/mcp/backend.ts
Single daemon

On start it probes an existing
daemon's /api/health (800ms) and
reuses its port and token if alive.
Source: src/server/daemon.ts

Outside this view: Hosted relay path for iPads off the LAN (relay/, src/server/relay.ts); Model-drawn quick map via Claude API
(src/interpret/).
